column.text: Bitcoin is holding $81.6K support, and the line that matters today is $80.5K. Lose it and the crowded long side gets forced out, which breaks the bullish thesis. Hold it and the setup tilts toward a squeeze. Positioning is lopsided. The BTC long/short ratio sits at 2.19 on the retail side, while Hyperliquid whales are net short $215M of BTC and $252M of ETH. ETF flows are the bulls' main support. BTC took in +$137.3M on Wednesday 28 Oct, with a 7-day net of +$201.8M. ETH was the weak spot, with Wednesday at −$21.4M and a 7-day net of −$287.5M. SOL bled too, at −$5.7M on Wednesday and −$43.6M over 7 days. Liquidations ran $335M–$338M over 24h as Bitcoin slipped back below $80,000 alongside the tech selloff. Macro offers no help. The Fed paused at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10-2 vote, Chair Warsh said inflation is too high, and September Core PCE printed 3.1%. Dollar liquidity is flat, so trade the structure, not a macro story. The regime is RISK_OFF. A down-trending tape is not a short signal by itself. Shorts need a mechanism you can point to in the printed data, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20d MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. Counter-trend longs only at clear exhaustion with a catalyst. HYPE broke $94 and sits 4.3% from its all-time high, helped by ICE moving to bring Hyperliquid perps to US retail. Fear & Greed reads 51, neutral. Watch $80.5K. A clean break turns the squeeze thesis into a liquidation trade.
